intent: Address the early off-track exits seen in the baseline (one line loss per run, max_error at the 0.06 m limit, progress about 0.15). Widen the sensor span to ±0.045 m so the array keeps the tape in view out to about 0.06 m offset, and narrow the wheel track to 0.10 m to add turn authority. Keep the footprint, body, mass and wheel radius unchanged so the effect of these two changes can be read cleanly in the next race.
learning: Baseline (iteration 0) showed that runs end by off-track exit after about one line loss, with rms error low and max error at the 0.06 m limit. The line is lost once the robot is about 0.05 m off centre, because the sensor array only reaches about ±0.036 m. Next iteration: check whether line_loss_events falls to 0 and whether max_error drops below 0.05 m. If the robot now finishes oval or s-bend, the sensing reach was the constraint. If it still exits with a line loss, turn authority is the constraint, so try mass 0.6 kg.
rationale: The development evidence (entityR2A) is the only race data so far, from the iteration 0 baseline. Every one of 60 trials went off track and none finished: progress was only 0.11 to 0.18, and each run had about one line-loss event. Tracking error is small while the robot is on the line (rms 0.021 to 0.030 m), but max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.063 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. So the robot is not wandering; it drifts to the edge of the allowed band and loses the tape. Line loss means no sensor sees the tape. With sensors at ±0.03 m and a 12 mm footprint, the array covers only about ±0.036 m, so once the robot is roughly 0.05 m off centre the tape falls outside every sensor, and the off-track limit at 0.06 m ends the run shortly after. Steering oscillation is low (0.11 to 0.15), so the robot is not over-reacting; it is failing to recover in time. Body width cannot relax the limit, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 for any allowed width. The levers are sensing reach and turn authority. I widen the outer sensors to ±0.045 m with 22.5 mm steps, so the array still sees the tape at 0.05 to 0.06 m offset and the controller gets an earlier, larger signal. I narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, which raises yaw rate for the same wheel differential (turn rate = wheel speed difference / wheel_track), so the robot can turn back before reaching the limit. I keep the 12 mm footprint, which is well inside the 25 mm tape, and keep mass 0.8 kg, because oscillation is not a problem. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, lower max_error, and the first completed runs on oval and s-bend. Slalom may still be hard. If line_loss_events stays at 1 with max_error near 0.06, the next step is turn authority: lower mass to about 0.6 kg to cut yaw inertia.
